english.title: Knowingly / recklessly retain personal data without consent of controller
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) after obtaining personal data, knowingly or recklessly retained it without the consent of the person who was the controller in relation to that data at the time it was obtained
english.legislation: Contrary to section 170(1)(c) and 196(2) of the Data Protection Act 2018.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

english.notes:
(i) Prosecution only by the Commissioner or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii) Where this offence has been committed by a body corporate, and it is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of or to be attributable to neglect on the part of a director, manager, secretary or similar officer of the body corporate, or a person who was purporting to act in such a capacity, the director, manager, secretary, as well as the body corporate is guilty of the offence and proceedings can also be taken against them.
(iii) It is a defence for a person charged with this offence to prove that it was necessary for preventing or detecting crime, was required or authorised by law or was in the public interest - see section 170(2) for details of this defence.
(iv) It is a defence for a person charged with this offence to prove that they reasonable believed they had a legal right or would have had the consent of the controller, or, that they acted for special purposes, journalistic reasons or in the public interest - see section 170(3) for details of this defence.
(v) Section 199(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018 states that the National Police Records (Recordable Offences) Regulations 2000 (S.I. 2000/1139) has effect as if this offence was listed in the Schedule to the Regulations. Therefore offenders must be fingerprinted and photographed as well as the offence being PNC recordable.
